items.label: Build-less vanilla JS + CSS custom properties
items.recommendation: Keep the console build-less: vanilla JS state/render + CSS custom properties for tokens, and hand-authored SVG/CSS micro-visuals. The corpus' no-framework chart (uPlot) and SVG/CSS craft sources demonstrate the approach at this scale. The choice itself is a [P] local guardrail (r0 §9.8); the corpus shows viable alternatives, not proof React is unnecessary.
items.when: A single-page local operator console with no npm pipeline.
items.avoid_when: Many contributors needing a typed component model.

items.recommendation: Use line/area marks for trends over time and sparklines inline in rows; this is the single most-evidenced mark family in the corpus.

items.recommendation: Encode many nodes' state as a status grid so color/position read pre-attentively; NN/g's dashboard guidance and Grafana's panel model both support grid-over-list at fleet scale.

items.avoid_when: A handful of records better shown as cards.

items.label: Smallest viable token layer (CSS custom properties)
items.recommendation: Define one token set (surface/elevation/accent/status/type) with CSS custom properties and derive variants with color-mix(); this is the smallest design-system layer that yields consistency without a framework runtime.
items.when: A single-page console needs visual consistency.
items.avoid_when: Tokens proliferate without a naming convention.

items.label: Colorblind-safe, never-color-alone status
items.recommendation: Keep status hues few and colorblind-safe, and always pair color with shape/label; contrast + palette sources (web.dev, ColorBrewer, NN/g, WCAG 1.4.3) define the bar.
items.when: Lifecycle/severity/attention states are encoded.
items.avoid_when: Hue count grows until it is noise.

items.label: Dark-first with a real light + forced-colors path
items.recommendation: Theme dark-first but keep a real light theme from the same tokens, and honor prefers-color-scheme/forced-colors; NN/g's dark-mode guidance and MDN's forced-colors feature define the fallback.
items.when: The room is dark by default.
items.avoid_when: Dark is just inverted light (elevation/contrast break).

items.label: Accent economy / minimal chrome
items.recommendation: Spend the accent color on one thing at a time and strip decorative chrome; Refactoring UI and NN/g both argue restrained accents carry more meaning.
items.when: Data is dense and chrome competes with it.
items.avoid_when: Every panel is highlighted (nothing stands out).

items.avoid_when: More than a few sizes / weights are in play.

items.label: One icon family, labelled where ambiguous
